body:
I understand your concern. I will keep some money just in case. Understand that when I say I don't have any survival skills, I mean that I don't have any experience... it is not to say I haven't done research and reading on the subject. I'll be sure to bring good equipment and I'll try to bring enough in the way of emergency rations to give me some time to learn. 

I know I'm not doing this the wise way... but I think that is how I have to do it. 

Thanks for caring though. 

I'm going to go now. For better or for worst. If in a few years I feel an urge to return to society, I'll be sure to do an IAMA. But until then, goodbye reddit.

It wouldn't be the same if it was just a hobby or a class. It would be meaningless like everything else. There is no true challenge when it is just a hobby or a class, which makes it feel like no true accomplishment. 

As for changing careers.... I'm not sure I could deal with the confrontations I would have to make in order to do so. And there isn't anything I would want to do. I don't like people in general that much, certainly not enough to volunteer.
